sections.html:
Parkland sits in Broward's northwest corner, and its buyers usually want acreage, quiet streets and newer construction. Its boundaries are State Road 7 on the east, the Everglades on the west, the Sawgrass Expressway on the south and Loxahatchee Road on the north.

A cattle farmer founded the city in 1963 after buying over 1,000 acres of Everglades land with his father, then sold plots off his ranch. Roads stayed unpaved into the 1980s, and some areas still feel rural. Growth since then runs from under 100 residents on 420 acres to nearly 38,000 on more than 8,000 acres.

Many lots are large, a few back onto horse or trail corridors, and the age and look of the homes change from street to street. Investors paying cash tend to focus on roof, drainage and permit history rather than finishes, so collect those records first.

sections.h2: Sale routes for a Parkland owner
sections.html:
You can list with a broker, go it alone, or take a direct cash purchase. Your calendar and repair budget usually decide.

  • Brokered listing: reaches the most buyers, but means prep, showings and waiting on a loan.
  • Private sale: no commission, but pricing, the contract and disclosures are on you.
  • Direct cash purchase: fast and as is, at a price that reflects repair and resale risk.

Compare offers by the amount left in your pocket once repairs, taxes, fees and carrying costs are paid, and read the whole contract first. A newer roof and clean permits help on all three routes.

Building permits and occupancy certificates come from the Building Department inside City Hall at 6600 University Drive, phone 954.753.5447. The office keeps Monday to Thursday hours, 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM.

Contractors now apply through the city's online portal and must re-register with new insurance and license documents. Fees changed starting October 1, 2025 under a city resolution, so request the current schedule from the department before you plan repairs.

An unclosed permit for an old roof, window or addition can hold up a closing. Find out what the department has on file for your lot before you market the house.

Florida sets the calendar and Broward offices follow it. January 1 is the valuation date, March 1 is the exemption deadline, and bills arrive in November.

  • Early payment pays: 4 percent off in November, then one point less each month through February.
  • A bill still unpaid on April 1 is delinquent.
  • A permanent residence can get up to $50,000 of homestead exemption if it was occupied that way on January 1.

Once the house sells, it is reassessed at just value the next January, and the new owner may owe much more than you. Leave your own bill out of the sales pitch. The Broward property appraiser's number is 954-357-6830.

Deeds in Broward carry a documentary stamp tax at a single rate. The contract may name who pays, but under state rules everyone on the deed remains liable.

Florida deed and recording charges
ChargeRate
Doc stamps on the deed$0.70 per $100 of price
Doc stamps on a mortgage35 cents per $100 borrowed
Recording, page one$5.00, then $4.00 for each added page
Names past the fourth$1.00 each

The clerk collects at recording. Your closing agent can put these rates against your real price in a written estimate.

sections.h2: Inherited house or behind on payments
sections.html:
Both follow set legal steps. For a modest estate, summary administration is open when non-exempt assets are $150,000 or less, or when the death was more than two years ago.

After a foreclosure judgment, the auction is set roughly three to five weeks out, though the lender can agree to a later date. Money from the sale above the debt may be claimable, and homestead owners are told to ask the clerk within 10 days. A sale beforehand can protect equity, so speak with an attorney and your lender.

  • Gather the deed, your newest tax bill and all lender letters.
  • Ask the Broward clerk's office which filings touch the property.
  • Request a payoff statement before weighing offers.

sections.h2: When a tax bill goes unpaid
sections.html:
April 1 starts delinquency, and by June 1 the county sells certificates against the unpaid tax. Once two years pass from April 1 of the issue year, the certificate holder may apply for a tax deed and pays $75 to do it.

The tax collector then identifies who must get notice: the titleholder, lienholders and any contract for deed buyer. Selling before an application is filed keeps your options open if you are behind. Request a current payoff figure from the Broward tax collector's office.

  • A homestead owner over 65 may defer part of the bill on Form DR-570, due March 31.
  • To prepay in installments, apply by May 1.
  • Whether to accept a partial payment is up to the collector.

Stamp tax applies to a quitclaim, and for Save Our Homes it is a change of ownership unless an exception, such as a transfer between spouses, fits. Handing the house to a relative before a sale can lift the tax base and add stamp tax.

A lady bird deed is treated differently: a revenue advisement found no present beneficial interest passed on the facts it reviewed. See an attorney before you record any of these.

Parkland has 11 parks with trails for families, dogs and horses, a library, and a Native American midden more than 1,000 years old. Buyers who want room like trails and horse access, so say so if your lot backs onto one. Check park and school boundaries yourself before advertising them.

sections.h2: Selling a house with a tenant
sections.html:
When rent is unpaid, the landlord serves a written 3 day demand that skips weekends and court holidays. Other curable lease problems get a 7 day window.

Ending a month by month tenancy takes 30 days' notice. Read the lease before selling an occupied house, since a sale does not cancel it. Show buyers the lease and rent history early, and warn the tenant before any showing or inspection.

sections.h2: What to have ready before you list
sections.html: Pull together your deed, the newest tax bill, notes on the roof and drainage, and the permit file from the Building Department. Ask your lender for a payoff statement if you still owe. Clear records let a cash buyer move fast, and the closing agent can start title work as soon as you sign. An open permit should be closed out or disclosed, not left for the inspector to find. Walk the lot too: with larger parcels, buyers look hard at fencing, drainage swales and any outbuilding, and a short list of what is permitted and what is not saves arguments later.

faqs.q: Which office runs the tax timeline for a Parkland home?
faqs.a: The state sets the calendar and Broward offices apply it: value on January 1, exemption filing through March 1, bills in November, delinquency from April 1.

faqs.q: Does paying cash remove doc stamp tax in Parkland?
faqs.a: No. The stamp tax is $0.70 per $100 of price however you pay, and all parties on the deed are liable. Decide who covers it in the contract.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Parkland house with open permits?
faqs.a: You can, but it complicates things. The Building Department at 954.753.5447 can tell you which permits are still open on your lot, and buyers and title companies will look.

faqs.q: What happens to my homestead exemption when I sell?
faqs.a: It ends at the sale. The buyer is assessed at just value beginning the following January.

faqs.q: How soon can an inherited Parkland house be sold?
faqs.a: That depends on the court path. Estates with non-exempt assets up to $150,000 can use summary administration, while larger or contested ones need formal administration, so see a probate attorney.
